newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares rise, trade thin for Western Easter.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares rise, trade thin for Western Easter.

text.p: Leading Russian shares rallied on Monday on light volumes as Western players stayed away for the Easter holiday, and traders said the market would keep its upward trend throughout the week on domestic speculation.
On the Micex Interbank Currency Exchange the rouble was unchanged at 5,727 to the dollar. Dealers expected demand for roubles to rise before new auctions for government securities later this week.
The Russian Trading System (RTS) 23-share index rose 1.3 percent to 301.30. But trade volume was just $17 million in the absence of foreign players.
Traders said the low volumes meant domestic speculation was the main reason for the rally.
"Russian players are trying to use the absence of foreign investors to speculate," said Renaissance trader Vladimir Tchikikvadze.

Traders said electric company UES EESR.RTS benefited from the speculation, edging up to $0.1917 on $2.7 million traded from Friday's close at $0.1885. The government has announced plans to restructure it the giant company.
"UES didn't go down because domestic traders saw they could buy cheaply," said Oleg Martynenko, chief of Rossiisky Credit Bank's Equity Sales and Trading.
Regional utility Mosenergo, LUKoil and Gazprom closed slightly higher.
Traders said the market would continue to be dominated by domestic players for the coming week as Western investors concentrated primarily on other markets.
"I see a nervous market with an upward trend but with periodic falls in prices," Martynenko said.
